overview.description: A new authenticated API endpoint has been implemented to retrieve all images stored in S3 for the current user. This endpoint supports pagination, filtering by folder prefix, and optional signed URL generation for secure access.
overview.purpose: Enable the frontend to display user-uploaded images, browse media galleries, and integrate image selection into existing workflows (post creation, profile management, inspiration boards, etc.).
overview.backend-status: Implemented, tested, and deployed to staging environment.

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: Maximum number of items to return per request

parameter.name: cursor
parameter.description: Pagination cursor token returned from previous response (nextCursor field). Omit for first page.

parameter.name: prefix
parameter.description: Optional sub-folder filter under user's root folder. Examples: "covers/", "accounts/", "inspirations/" Leave empty to retrieve all user images.

parameter.name: signed
parameter.description: When true, generates presigned URLs for secure, temporary access to images. Use this if S3 bucket is private or for enhanced security.

parameter.name: expiresIn
parameter.description: Signed URL expiration time in seconds (1 minute to 24 hours). Only used when signed=true.

field.name: url
field.description: Public S3 URL for the image

field.name: contentType
field.description: MIME type (currently not populated, reserved for future use)

field.name: nextCursor
field.description: Continuation token for fetching the next page. Only present when hasMore=true.

field.name: hasMore
field.description: Indicates whether more results are available. When true, use nextCursor to fetch the next page.

error.description: Server error or S3 connection failure

requirement.description: Create a new API service method for fetching user images
requirement.acceptance: Method should handle authentication, query parameters, and response parsing. Should follow existing API client patterns in the codebase.

requirement.description: Define TypeScript interfaces for request params and response data
requirement.acceptance: Types should match the API specification exactly. Use proper optional fields for signedUrl, nextCursor, etc.

requirement.description: Implement infinite scroll or "Load More" functionality
requirement.acceptance: Use nextCursor from previous response to fetch next page. Handle hasMore flag to show/hide load more button. Prevent duplicate items when loading more pages.

requirement.description: Handle all error scenarios gracefully with user-friendly messages
requirement.acceptance: Show appropriate error messages for 401, 400, 500 errors. Provide retry mechanism for failed requests. Log errors for debugging purposes.

requirement.description: Implement progressive image loading with placeholders
requirement.acceptance: Show skeleton/spinner while images are loading. Handle broken images gracefully. Optimize for performance with lazy loading if needed.

requirement.description: Implement appropriate caching strategy for image lists
requirement.acceptance: Consider using React Query, SWR, or similar for data caching. Implement cache invalidation when new images are uploaded. Balance between fresh data and performance.

requirement.description: Create a responsive image gallery component
requirement.acceptance: Display images in a grid layout (responsive: 1-4 columns based on screen size). Show image metadata (size, date) on hover or in detail view. Support image selection for downstream actions.
Provide tabs or dropdown to filter by prefix (All, Covers, Accounts, Inspirations, etc.). Update URL params when filter changes for shareable links. Show empty state when no images match filter.

requirement.description: Implement clear loading and empty states
requirement.acceptance: Show skeleton loaders during initial load. Show spinner for pagination requests. Display friendly empty state when user has no images. Provide call-to-action to upload first image.

requirement.description: Add contextual actions for each image
requirement.acceptance: Support image selection (single or multi-select). Provide preview/lightbox functionality. Add "Copy URL" action for easy sharing. Consider delete action (requires separate backend endpoint).
Touch-friendly image selection. Optimized grid layout for small screens. Smooth infinite scroll on mobile devices. Consider mobile-specific gestures (pinch to zoom, swipe).

step.title: Define TypeScript Types
step.description: Create TypeScript interfaces for the API request and response. Place in appropriate types/models directory.

step.title: Create API Service Method
step.description: Add a new method to the existing API client for fetching user images. Use existing authentication and error handling patterns.

step.title: Create React Hook (Optional but Recommended)
step.description: Create a custom hook using React Query or SWR for data fetching and caching. This provides automatic refetching, caching, and loading states.

step.title: Create Image Gallery Component
step.description: Build a reusable image gallery component with grid layout and responsive design.

step.title: Add Folder Filter UI
step.description: Create a filter/tab component to switch between different image folders.

step.title: Implement Error Handling
step.description: Add proper error handling with user-friendly messages and retry logic.

step.title: Add Loading and Empty States
step.description: Create skeleton loaders and empty state components for better UX.

step.title: Add Unit Tests
step.description: Write tests for the API service, hooks, and components.

integration-point.name: Post Creation Flow
integration-point.description: Allow users to select existing uploaded images when creating posts, instead of always uploading new ones.

integration-point.name: Profile Management
integration-point.description: Display user's uploaded account avatars in profile settings, allow selection of existing avatar.

integration-point.name: Inspiration Board
integration-point.description: Show user's saved inspiration images in a gallery view.

integration-point.name: Media Library
integration-point.description: Create a dedicated "Media Library" page showing all user images with advanced filtering, sorting, and management capabilities.

test-case.title: Fetch images with default parameters
test-case.steps: 1. Open the image gallery 2. Verify API is called with default params (limit=50, no cursor) 3. Verify images are displayed in grid layout
test-case.expected: Images load successfully with default settings

test-case.title: Pagination - Load more
test-case.steps: 1. Load initial page with limit=10 2. Click "Load More" button 3. Verify nextCursor is sent in second request 4. Verify new images are appended (no duplicates)
test-case.expected: Pagination works correctly, no duplicate images

test-case.title: Filter by folder/prefix
test-case.steps: 1. Select "Cover Images" filter 2. Verify API is called with prefix=covers/ 3. Verify only cover images are displayed
test-case.expected: Filter correctly limits results to selected folder

test-case.title: Signed URLs
test-case.steps: 1. Enable signed URLs (signed=true) 2. Verify images load using signedUrl field 3. Verify URLs contain signature parameters
test-case.expected: Signed URLs are generated and used correctly

test-case.title: Empty state
test-case.steps: 1. Test with user who has no uploaded images 2. Verify empty state component is shown 3. Verify call-to-action button is present
test-case.expected: Friendly empty state shown when no images exist

test-case.title: Error handling - 401 Unauthorized
test-case.steps: 1. Clear authentication token 2. Attempt to load images 3. Verify 401 error is caught 4. Verify user is prompted to sign in
test-case.expected: User is redirected to login or shown auth error

test-case.title: Error handling - 500 Server Error
test-case.steps: 1. Mock server error response 2. Verify error state is shown 3. Verify retry button is available 4. Click retry and verify request is sent again
test-case.expected: Error handled gracefully with retry option

test-case.title: Image selection
test-case.steps: 1. Click on an image 2. Verify selection state is updated 3. Verify onImageSelect callback is triggered 4. Test multi-select if enabled

test-case.title: Mobile responsiveness
test-case.steps: 1. Open on mobile device or resize browser 2. Verify grid adapts to smaller screen 3. Verify touch interactions work 4. Test infinite scroll on mobile
test-case.expected: Gallery is fully functional on mobile devices

test-case.title: Performance - Large result sets
test-case.steps: 1. Test with user who has 500+ images 2. Verify initial load is fast (only fetches limit) 3. Verify pagination doesn't cause memory issues 4. Verify images lazy load appropriately
test-case.expected: Performance remains good with large datasets

consideration.title: Image Optimization
consideration.description: Consider using next/image or similar for automatic image optimization. Implement lazy loading for images not in viewport.

consideration.title: Caching Strategy
consideration.description: Use React Query or SWR for automatic caching and revalidation. Set appropriate stale times (5-10 minutes recommended). Implement cache invalidation when user uploads new images.

consideration.title: Pagination Size
consideration.description: Balance between fewer requests (larger limit) and faster initial load (smaller limit). Recommended: 20-30 items per page for grid layouts.

consideration.title: Signed URL Expiration
consideration.description: Choose appropriate expiration time based on use case. For gallery view: 1 hour (3600s) is sufficient. For long-lived pages: Consider shorter expiration with auto-refresh.

consideration.title: Signed URLs vs Public URLs
consideration.description: Use signed=true if S3 bucket is private or for sensitive images. Use signed=false (public URLs) for better performance if images are public.

consideration.title: URL Exposure
consideration.description: Be cautious about storing signed URLs in browser storage. Signed URLs expire, so avoid long-term caching. Don't log or expose signed URLs in client-side error tracking.

consideration.title: Rate Limiting
consideration.description: Implement client-side rate limiting or debouncing for pagination requests. Prevent users from spamming the API.

Custom React hook for data fetching (useUserImages)
ImageGallery component with responsive grid layout
Pagination implementation (infinite scroll or load more)
Unit tests for services and components
Integration tests for key user flows

notes.note: The backend endpoint is already deployed and tested. Frontend can start integration immediately.
Consider creating a reusable ImagePicker component that can be used across multiple features (post creation, profile settings, etc.).
If implementing signed URLs, be aware that they expire. Plan for graceful handling when signed URLs expire while user is viewing the gallery.
The API automatically filters to only return image file types. Frontend doesn't need additional filtering logic.
Consider adding image metadata display (size, dimensions, upload date) in a detail view or tooltip for better user experience.
